- **Denial audits roll back.** Denial audit events (purpose binding, child block) are written in the caller's
  transaction, so they are lost when the caller rolls back. A separate denial transaction, as in sangam-security,
  is not done here because of the ROOT_SEQ deadlock risk.
- **Denial audits (SL-137, M-009), closed in code 2026-11-12.** `CMP_PURPOSE_BINDING_DENIED` and
  `CMP_CHILD_PROCESSING_BLOCKED` go to a denial-only chain `cmp:d:<32 hex>` per data principal (`ComplianceAudit`) and
  commit on their own through the leaf pool `sangam-compliance-audit` (`ComplianceWiring`; property
  `sangam.compliance.denial-audit.pool.maximum-size`, default 2; it is derived from the main HikariCP pool and refuses
  to start without one). So a denial survives the caller's rollback, and neither the main pool (SL-43) nor the
  caller's `ROOT_SEQ` row is waited on. Every refused attempt writes one event. Tests `DenialAuditSurvivesRollbackH2Test`
  and `ComplianceDenialAuditPoolTest` (sangam-server) are written and not run yet. Pool sizing: deploy README §1.6.
